papers.title: Ultrasound diagnosis of adenomyosis: new technologies – new approaches
papers.abstract: To date, one of the most common endometriosis types is uterine endometriosis (adenomyosis). Persistent adenomyosis in older age is followed by worsening of complaints associated with a high frequency of chronic pelvic pain syndrome, menorrhagia, abnormal uterine bleeding, and dyspareunia. Objective. To determine the efficacy of two- and three-dimensional ultrasound in the diagnosis of adenomyosis in patients in the late reproductive and perimenopausal periods. Patients and methods. A total of 143 patients with adenomyosis were included in the study and divided into two groups: group 1 – 65 patients in the late reproductive period, group 2 – 78 patients in the perimenopause. The thickness, volume and structure of the endometrium, qualitative hemodynamic parameters of uterine terminal vessels were determined in 2D mode. In 3D mode, volumetric indices of blood flow in the endometrium and sub-endometrium were calculated. Results. Adenomyosis in the late reproductive and perimenopausal periods is associated with changes in the morpho-functional state of the endometrium due to elevated blood flow resistance in uterine terminal vessels. The vascularization index (VI) should be considered the most objective 3D blood flow parameter. Conclusion. A comprehensive 2D/3D ultrasound is a reliable method of adenomyosis diagnosis in patients in the late reproductive and perimenopausal periods. 3D ultrasound is an additional objective method to assess the endometrial volume and hemodynamics in the terminal branches of the radial artery. Key words: adenomyosis, three-dimensional ultrasound, junctional zone

papers.title: Comprehensive method of ultrasound diagnosis of adenomyosis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: There are currently no uniform standards for adenomyosis diagnosis, so the search for the most informative methods is an urgent task. This article presents modern views on the diagnosis of adenomyosis and the role of ultrasound in its diagnostics. AIM: The aim of this study was to determine the diagnostic capabilities of ultrasound in the diffuse form of adenomyosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 164 patients aged 22 to 43 years old, who had a comprehensive ultrasound examination done. The points were calculated and the presence or absence of adenomyosis, as well as its severity, were determined using the developed scale. The sequential implementation of six ultrasound techniques were used for a comprehensive ultrasound assessment of adenomyosis: assessment of the myometrium echostructure homogeneity; assessment of the ratio of the anterior and posterior uterine wall thicknesses; compression elastography; assessment of the junctional zone in the 3D mode; assessment of the uniformity of the junctional zone thickness along uterine walls; vascularization of the myometrium in the Power Doppler 3D Glass Body mode. RESULTS: We have developed the comprehensive ultrasound method of adenomyosis diagnostics. The sensitivity of the method was 95%, and the specificity was 100%. The positive predictive value was 100%, and the negative predictive value was 90%. The accuracy of the method was 97%. CONCLUSIONS: The developed scoring system for the comprehensive assessment of adenomyosis allows for an independent assessment of the myometrium for each criterion, summarizing the scores and, therefore, assessing the presence and severity of adenomyosis more objectively and reliably. The high sensitivity and specificity of this technique allows recommending it for use by ultrasound specialists.

papers.title: Accurate Structure Prediction of Biomolecular Interactions with AlphaFold 3
papers.abstract: Introduces a unified generative diffusion architecture capable of predicting joint 3D coordinates for complexes including proteins, nucleic acids (DNA/RNA), small molecule ligands, and chemical modifications.
papers.researchQuestion: Can a single deep generative diffusion network predict atomic-resolution coordinates of heterogeneous multi-molecule complexes without dedicated physics-based docking approximations?
papers.methodology: Couples a Pairformer representation network with a direct 3D Cartesian coordinate diffusion module to progressively denoise spatial structures across all biological molecule classes.
papers.results: Substantially exceeds classical molecular docking packages on standardized protein-ligand and protein-nucleic acid benchmark evaluations (e.g., PoseBusters).
papers.limitations: Static single-state coordinate predictions do not sample full kinetic conformational ensembles or solve arbitrary disordered loop transitions.
papers.conclusion: Unified generative diffusion frameworks provide a shared foundational platform for structural biology across the broader chemical spectrum of life.

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of transvaginal ultrasound for adenomyosis using consensus-based direct and indirect sonographic signs: prospective cohort study
papers.abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Objective
                    To evaluate the diagnostic performance of transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) for adenomyosis using consensus‐based direct and indirect ultrasound signs, with histopathology as the reference standard.
                  
                  
                    Methods
                    This prospective diagnostic accuracy study included women undergoing TVS examination at a tertiary referral center (Hospital San Juan de Dios, Santiago, Chile) between 1 December 2022 and 1 December 2023. Women aged ≥ 18 years who underwent hysterectomy within 6 months after TVS examination were enrolled consecutively. Cases with malignant histopathological findings were excluded. Ultrasound signs of adenomyosis were assessed according to the revised Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment consensus. Histopathology served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance measures for individual ultrasound features and multivariable models were calculated.
                  
                  
                    Results
                    Among 2967 women evaluated using TVS, 345 (11.6%) underwent hysterectomy within 6 weeks and constituted the study cohort. Histopathology confirmed adenomyosis in 155 (44.9%) women. Individual ultrasound features showed high specificity but limited sensitivity. Among direct signs, echogenic subendometrial lines showed the best overall balance (sensitivity, 53.5% (95% CI, 45.4–61.6%); specificity, 94.7% (95% CI, 90.5–97.4%)). Individual indirect signs showed specificity > 97% but low sensitivity. A model combining direct ultrasound signs showed high specificity (93.7% (95% CI, 89.2–96.7%)) but limited sensitivity (60.0% (95% CI, 51.8–67.8%)); overall diagnostic accuracy was 78.6% (95% CI, 73.8–82.8%). The addition of indirect ultrasound signs into the model did not provide meaningful incremental benefit.
                  
                  
                    Conclusions
                    Our findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between direct and indirect ultrasound features, with direct signs providing the most consistent diagnostic value, while indirect signs should be interpreted as supportive rather than definitive. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.abstract: Proposes the Transformer architecture, replacing recurrent and convolutional layers with multi-head self-attention mechanisms to establish direct dependencies across arbitrary token distances in sequence processing with high GPU parallelization.
papers.journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 30)
papers.researchQuestion: Can sequence-to-sequence dependencies be effectively mapped in constant computational path length without sequential recurrent or convolutional constraints?
papers.methodology: Stacked encoder-decoder multi-head dot-product attention modules with fixed sinusoidal positional encodings, residual connections, and layer normalization.
papers.results: Outperformed contemporary recurrent baselines on WMT 2014 translation tasks (28.4 BLEU English-German, 41.8 BLEU English-French) with substantially reduced training time.
papers.limitations: Quadratic O(N²) memory scaling relative to input token sequence length and fixed positional encoding extrapolation limits.
papers.conclusion: Self-attention mechanisms alone suffice for sequence transduction, establishing a parallelizable foundation for modern generative language modeling.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.abstract: Proposes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), coupling parametric neural sequence-to-sequence representations with dense vector document retrieval from external knowledge corpora to reduce factual hallucinations.
papers.journal: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
papers.researchQuestion: How can deep language models ground generative responses in external factual sources to reduce hallucination and provide verifiable source citations?
papers.methodology: Combines dense passage retrieval (DPR) over indexed document vectors with a sequence-to-sequence language generator (BART), optimizing end-to-end marginal likelihood over latent documents.
papers.results: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on knowledge-intensive open-domain question answering benchmarks (Natural Questions, WebQuestions) with verifiable citation provenance.
papers.limitations: Retrieval roundtrips add compute latency, and external corpus vector indexes require synchronization and periodic re-embedding.
papers.conclusion: Augmenting parametric neural weights with non-parametric retrieval significantly mitigates factual errors and establishes an empirical foundation for zero-hallucination systems.

papers.title: Application of multimodal ultrasound radiomics in the diagnosis of superficial lymph node tuberculosis
papers.abstract: "Objective: To develop preoperative diagnostic models for superficial lymph node tuberculosis (LNTB) using radiomic features extracted from multimodal ultrasound imaging, including gray-scale ultrasound (US), ultrasound elastography (UE), and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), in conjunction with various machine learning algorithms.Methods: A retrospective study was conducted on 222 patients with lymphadenopathy. The patients were randomly divided into a training group ($n=156$) and a validation group ($n=66$) in a 7:3 ratio. 837 radiomics features were extracted from images of each modality (US, UE and CEUS). After initial screening by hypothesis testing, the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with five-fold cross-validation was used for feature dimensionality reduction and selection. After feature selection, five machine learning models—logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, support vector machine, and AdaBoost—were used to construct radiomic-based models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the area under the curve (AUC) was computed to assess the performance of each model in predicting superficial LNTB. Clinical decision curve (DCA) is used to measure the net benefits under various probability thresholds. The diagnostic performance of ultrasound physicians was also compared with that of the best-performing machine learning model.Results: Among the models generated by different algorithms, the decision tree model exhibited the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.909 (95% CI, 0.789–0.949) in the training cohort and 0.866 (95% CI, 0.774–0.958) in the validation cohort. The AUC, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) for ultrasound physicians were 0.693 (95% CI, 0.568–0.818), 0.698, 0.689, 0.722, and 0.664, respectively. The DCA shows that the decision tree model has the best net income in the range of clinical relevance threshold of 0.6–0.8. Delong test showed that decision tree model was superior to ultrasonic doctor's diagnosis ($Z=2.98$, $p<0.0029$).Conclusion: The radiomic model constructed from US, UE, and CEUS demonstrated robust diagnostic performance for superficial LNTB, with the decision tree model yielding the best results
papers.researchQuestion: "This study aims to develop a radiomic model using multimodal ultrasound imaging to predict superficial LNTB preoperatively, and further construct single-modal subgroup models to evaluate the diagnostic value of different modal combinations, providing a potential early diagnostic tool adaptable to different clinical practice conditions."
papers.methodology: "This retrospective study included patients with lymphadenopathy who presented to our hospital between September 2018 and September 2022... Ultrasound examinations were performed using Philips IU22 and IU-Elite ultrasound diagnostic machines, equipped with L12-5 and L9-3 broadband linear probes, with a frequency range of 3 to 12 MHz... Two physicians, each with over five years of experience in superficial lymph node ultrasound diagnosis and blinded to pathological results, manually delineated regions of interest (ROI) on the US, UE, and CEUS images using 3D Slicer software to obtain ROI mask files, which were saved in NRRD format. The segmented ROIs were then imported into Pyradiomics software to extract radiomic features. During model development, the synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) was applied to the training cohort to address potential class imbalance. In addition, all extracted features were normalized using Z-scores before feature selection and model construction... Patients were randomly divided into a training group and a validation group in a 7:3 ratio... Feature selection was performed using a two-step procedure. First, univariate hypothesis testing was applied to identify features that differed significantly between the LNTB and non-LNTB groups ($P<0.05$). The retained features were then further reduced using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with five-fold cross-validation... The optimal features were used to construct predictive models employing logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), and AdaBoost algorithms."
papers.results: "Among the models generated by different algorithms, the decision tree model exhibited the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.909 (95% CI, 0.789–0.949) in the training cohort and 0.866 (95% CI, 0.774–0.958) in the validation cohort. The AUC, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) for ultrasound physicians were 0.693 (95% CI, 0.568–0.818), 0.698, 0.689, 0.722, and 0.664, respectively. The DCA shows that the decision tree model has the best net income in the range of clinical relevance threshold of 0.6–0.8. Delong test showed that decision tree model was superior to ultrasonic doctor's diagnosis ($Z=2.98$, $p<0.0029$)... papers.limitations: "This study has several limitations: (1) it was a single-center, retrospective study with a limited sample size; (2) all ultrasound images were obtained using the same brand of ultrasound equipment, and it is unclear whether images from other manufacturers would show any biases; (3) a binary classification approach was used, and non-tuberculous lymphadenopathy was not further subdivided. Future research should include subgroup analyses to better differentiate between various non-tuberculous lymph node diseases; (4) all the patients in this study completed three-mode ultrasound, which avoided the disadvantage of lower diagnostic efficiency compared with the single-mode prediction model studied in the past. This may also lead to case selection bias, and prospective research will be carried out in the future to verify the generalization of the model; (5) a prospective targeted validation study will be carried out in the future, including specific clinical populations such as primary hospital patients with only US examination, immunocompromised patients (e.g., diabetes, HIV) with suspected LNTB, and pediatric patients with superficial lymphadenopathy, to further verify the model's diagnostic efficacy in different clinical scenarios.
papers.conclusion: Multimodal ultrasound-based radiomic models demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for superficial LNTB, with the decision tree model exhibiting the best performance. These models outperform traditional ultrasound diagnosis, offering valuable preoperative diagnostic support."

papers.title: The application of multimodal ultrasound examination in the differential diagnosis of benign and malignant breast lesions of BI-RADS category 4
papers.abstract:
"Objectives: The purpose of this study was to the diagnostic value of conventional ultrasound (US), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) and shear wave elastography (SWE) for identifying benign and malignant BI-RADS 4 breast lesions[cite: 8].

Materials and methods: From February 2022 to November 2024, 95 patients aged 20 to 90 years with breast diseases, all of whom were female, were included[cite: 8]. These lesions were diagnosed as BI-RADS 4 breast lesions by conventional ultrasound[cite: 8]. All lesions were pathologically confirmed by surgical resection or tissue biopsy, and they were further evaluated by CEUS and SWE[cite: 8]. The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and accuracy of US, CEUS, and SWE were statistically analyzed, and ROC curves were generated[cite: 8]. The diagnostic efficacy of US, US + SWE, US + CEUS, and US + CEUS + SWE were subsequently compared, with the pathology results used as the reference standard[cite: 8].

Results: (1) Among the 95 BI-RADS 4 lesions, 44 (46.31%) were benign, and 51 (53.69%) were malignant[cite: 8]. The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and accuracy of the BI-RADS classification via conventional US were 86.3, 72.7, 78.6, 82.1 and 80.0%, respectively[cite: 8]. (2) The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and accuracy of US combined with SWE in the diagnosis of breast nodules were 96.1, 79.5, 84.5, 94.6, and 88.4%, respectively[cite: 8]. (3) The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and accuracy of US combined with CEUS in the diagnosis of breast nodules were 84.3, 86.4, 87.8, 82.6, and 85.3%, respectively[cite: 8]. (4) The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of US, US + SWE and US + CEUS were 0.795, 0.877, and 0.917, respectively[cite: 8]. Statistical methods were used to evaluate the US + CEUS + SWE method, and the results indicated excellent diagnostic performance[cite: 8]. The AUC was 0.946, while the sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and accuracy were 90.7, 93.2, 94.2, 95.3, and 94.7%, respectively[cite: 8]...

Conclusion: (1) CEUS and SWE provide diagnostic information about the microvascular perfusion and tissue stiffness of lesions, respectively, which can assist in the differentiation of benign from malignant breast tumors by conventional US and improve the sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of diagnosis, especially for US BI-RADS 4a breast lesions[cite: 8]. (2) The combined use of CEUS and SWE in conventional US enhance the overall diagnostic performance with respect to breast lesions, with the best sensitivity and specificity and the highest diagnostic efficacy[cite: 8]. The use of US + CEUS + SWE is beneficial for further differentiating benign and malignant breast lesions according to the US BI-RADS 4, thereby reducing unnecessary biopsies or surgeries[cite: 8]."
papers.researchQuestion: "Therefore, the aim of this study was to explore the diagnostic efficacy of SWE, CEUS, and the combination of SWE and CEUS in conventional ultrasound to differentiate benign from malignant breast lesions[cite: 8]. We also investigated whether this can improve the sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of the BI-RADS 4 diagnosis, with pathology results used as the reference standard[cite: 8]."
papers.methodology: "This retrospective single-center study was approved by the local institutional review board and included 95 breast lesions (age range 20–90 years; mean 52.82 ± 3.47 years) between February 2022 to November 2024[cite: 8]... Prior to surgical excision, all subjects underwent conventional US, CEUS and SWE examinations[cite: 8]. The pathological results of the samples obtained by surgery or biopsy were regarded as the reference standard[cite: 8]... Mindray Resona R9 ultrasound diagnostic equipment equipped with L15-3WU linear array probes (frequency 3–15 MHz) and L9-3U linear array probes (frequency 3–9 MHz), as well as Mindray Resona 7 ultrasonic diagnostic equipment equipped with L14-5 linear array probes (frequency 5–14 MHz) and L9-3 linear array probes (frequency 3–9 MHz), was used...[cite: 8] All data were analyzed using SPSS 27.0 software[cite: 8]... The prediction model was built via the logistic equation[cite: 8]."
papers.results: "In total, 95 breast lesions were included in this study for the final analysis, among which 83 were solitary lesions and 6 were multiple lesions[cite: 8]... Among the 95 lesions, 46.3% (44/95) were benign, and 53.7% (51/95) were malignant[cite: 8]... The AUC of US + SWE + CEUS was considerably higher than that of US (0.946 vs. 0.795, $p<0.05$) and US + SWE (0.946 vs. 0.877, $p<0.05$)[cite: 8]. Furthermore, the AUC of US + SWE + CEUS was also greater than that of US + CEUS (0.946 vs. 0.917), but the difference was not significant[cite: 8]... The highest detection accuracy of 94.7% was achieved by US + SWE + CEUS[cite: 8]."
papers.limitations: "However, there may be some overlap in the elasticity coefficients of tissues under different conditions[cite: 8]. If the lesion is too deep (the distance from the leading edge of the lesion to the anterior edge of the breast skin is $\ge4$ cm) or if the lesion contains liquid components, or even internal calcification, it may lead to diagnostic bias in SWE[cite: 8]... Currently, although many studies on the ultrasonographic features of breast cancer using CEUS exist, the lack of a unified diagnostic standard has restricted its wide application in the diagnosis of breast diseases[cite: 8]... Further studies with larger sample sizes and higher sensitivity are needed to minimize false-negative results and confirm the reliability of this method in clinical settings[cite: 8]."
papers.conclusion: "(1) CEUS and SWE provide diagnostic information regarding the microvascular perfusion and tissue hardness of lesions, respectively[cite: 8]. The addition of CEUS and SWE to conventional US improves its diagnostic sensitivity, specificity and accuracy[cite: 8]. This is beneficial for further differentiation of benign and malignant lesions in US BI-RADS 4 cases, thus reducing unnecessary biopsies or surgeries[cite: 8]. Further studies with larger sample sizes and higher sensitivity are needed to minimize false-negative results and confirm the reliability of this method in clinical settings[cite: 8]."

papers.title: Ultrasound-Based Breast Cancer Classification Using Image-Based Features
papers.abstract: Objective: Evaluate machine learning classification of breast lesions on ultrasound imaging using extracted radiomics features. Methods: Retrospective cohort study analyzing B-mode ultrasound images. Results: The classification models achieved an accuracy of 0.84 on ultrasound images. Conclusion: Automated feature extraction provides high diagnostic accuracy for breast cancer classification.
papers.researchQuestion: Can machine learning classification of breast ultrasound features achieve high diagnostic accuracy?
papers.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing B-mode ultrasound images with automated feature extraction.
papers.results: The three best-performing breast lesion classification models achieved an accuracy of 0.84 on ultrasound images.
papers.conclusion: Automated feature extraction provides high diagnostic accuracy for breast cancer classification.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Evaluation of Ultrasound Images for Benign Skin Tumors
papers.abstract: Objective: To evaluate deep learning convolutional neural network algorithms for distinguishing benign skin tumors using high-resolution ultrasound imaging. Methods: Multi-center retrospective evaluation of skin lesion sonograms. Results: Deep learning achieved 0.89 sensitivity and 0.86 specificity. Conclusion: High-frequency ultrasound coupled with deep learning offers non-invasive assessment of benign cutaneous lesions.
papers.researchQuestion: Can deep learning algorithms distinguish benign skin tumors on high-frequency ultrasound?
papers.methodology: Convolutional neural networks trained on high-resolution sonographic images of benign cutaneous lesions.
papers.results: Deep learning models evaluated high-frequency ultrasound images of benign skin tumors, achieving 0.89 sensitivity and 0.86 specificity.
papers.limitations: Limited representation of rare histological subtypes.
papers.conclusion: High-frequency ultrasound coupled with deep learning provides robust non-invasive diagnosis of benign skin tumors.

chunks.text: Deep learning models evaluated high-frequency ultrasound images of benign skin tumors, achieving high diagnostic accuracy across epidermal cysts and seborrheic keratosis.
